paragraphs: Justinian handed the job to two teachers of geometry rather than a builder. Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus had written on mirrors, vaults and conic sections but had never raised anything close to this scale, and their dome sat flatter than its supports could safely carry. Earthquakes in 553 and 557 cracked it, and a third quake on the morning of 7 May 558 brought part of it down onto the altar and pulpit.

The repair went to Isidore's nephew, also named Isidore, who rebuilt the dome about six metres taller and added forty ribs to carry its weight down into the piers rather than out into the walls. The work finished in 562, and that steeper, ribbed dome has stood since, propped up over the centuries by buttresses that later Byzantine and Ottoman builders added to keep it up.
